name: Structural MRI (T1w/FLAIR)
signal_examples: T1-weighted (176 sagittal slices, 1mm3 voxels) and FLAIR (192 sagittal slices, 1mm3 voxels) structural sequences
citation: Anderson, E. J., Staples, R., Dyslin, S. M., Chang, E. H. T., Laks, A. B., Dickens, J. V., Mathur, D., Paul, S., Dvorak, E., & Turkeltaub, P. E. (2026). The Georgetown Reading in Aging Neuroimaging Dataset (GRAND) [Data set]. OpenNeuro. https://doi.org/10.18112/openneuro.ds007831.v1.0.1; Schwarz, C. G., Kremers, W. K., Therneau, T. M., et al. (2019). Identification of anonymous MRI research participants with face-recognition software. New England Journal of Medicine, 381(17), 1684-1686. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMc1908881
privacy_exit_point: A structural MRI volume can be used to reconstruct a recognizable 3D image of a participant's face; face-recognition software has been shown to re-identify supposedly de-identified research MRI scans specifically from this modality.
agency_control_point: A single standard sequence (T1w or FLAIR); a participant can decline or stop between sequences, but not part-way through one without the acquisition being discarded and, typically, redone.
notes: Illustrative gain/cost ratings, informed by GRAND's own acquisition parameters and by the cited re-identification finding - not values either source reports directly. Gain is moderate: structural volumes provide anatomical/morphometric context (e.g. atrophy, white-matter hyperintensity burden relevant in aging) but do not directly measure reading or language activity.

name: Functional MRI (T2*, language task)
signal_examples: T2* functional sequences (48 slices, 2.9mm voxels) during the Adaptive Language Mapping Task
citation: Anderson, E. J., Staples, R., Dyslin, S. M., Chang, E. H. T., Laks, A. B., Dickens, J. V., Mathur, D., Paul, S., Dvorak, E., & Turkeltaub, P. E. (2026). The Georgetown Reading in Aging Neuroimaging Dataset (GRAND) [Data set]. OpenNeuro. https://doi.org/10.18112/openneuro.ds007831.v1.0.1; Wilson, S. M., Yen, M., & Eriksson, D. K. (2018). An adaptive semantic matching paradigm for reliable and valid language mapping in individuals with aphasia. Human Brain Mapping, 39, 3285-3307. https://doi.org/10.1002/hbm.24077
privacy_exit_point: Lower spatial resolution than a structural scan and not by itself useful for facial reconstruction, but is typically co-registered to a structural volume for analysis, which can reintroduce identifiable anatomy indirectly.
agency_control_point: Requires active task performance (oral reading and lexical decision) for the duration of the scan; a participant can stop performing the task, but the running sequence continues acquiring until it completes.
notes: Illustrative gain/cost ratings, informed by GRAND's own task and acquisition parameters, not values GRAND reports directly. Gain is rated highest here: this is the modality that directly measures language-associated brain activity during reading, the closest measurement to the research question itself.

name: Diffusion MRI (HARDI/DTI)
signal_examples: HARDI diffusion-weighted imaging: 81 directions at b=3000, 40 directions at b=1200, 7 at b=0 (128 volumes total)
citation: Anderson, E. J., Staples, R., Dyslin, S. M., Chang, E. H. T., Laks, A. B., Dickens, J. V., Mathur, D., Paul, S., Dvorak, E., & Turkeltaub, P. E. (2026). The Georgetown Reading in Aging Neuroimaging Dataset (GRAND) [Data set]. OpenNeuro. https://doi.org/10.18112/openneuro.ds007831.v1.0.1
privacy_exit_point: Diffusion-weighted volumes are not by themselves useful for facial reconstruction, though they are acquired and stored alongside structural scans from the same session.
agency_control_point: The longest single raw sequence in this protocol (128 total diffusion-weighted and b=0 volumes); requires the participant to remain still for the longest continuous stretch of the session.
notes: Illustrative gain/cost ratings, informed by GRAND's own acquisition parameters, not values GRAND reports directly. Gain reflects white-matter tract integrity (e.g. the arcuate fasciculus) as a distinct axis from gray-matter structure (Structural) or activation (Functional) - how well reading- and language-relevant regions are physically connected, not whether they activate.

name: Connectome (derived)
signal_examples: Derived structural and/or functional connectome (network) summaries
citation: Anderson, E. J., Staples, R., Dyslin, S. M., Chang, E. H. T., Laks, A. B., Dickens, J. V., Mathur, D., Paul, S., Dvorak, E., & Turkeltaub, P. E. (2026). The Georgetown Reading in Aging Neuroimaging Dataset (GRAND) [Data set]. OpenNeuro. https://doi.org/10.18112/openneuro.ds007831.v1.0.1; Anderson, E. J. et al. (2026). The Georgetown Reading in Aging Neuroimaging Dataset (GRAND): Reading and multimodal MRI data in older adults. bioRxiv. https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.05.18.725986
privacy_exit_point: Not sensed directly - computed after the fact from diffusion and/or functional data already collected; a derived summary matrix carries far less identifying anatomical detail than a raw image volume.
agency_control_point: Requires no additional scanner time beyond the diffusion and/or functional sequences it is derived from.
notes: Illustrative gain/cost ratings; the lowest-documented modality here - GRAND's own README states the dataset 'includes DTI and derived connectomes,' but the parcellation/tractography pipeline used to build them is not detailed in the material checked for this page (the preprint's public abstract does not mention connectome construction). Gain is a moderate estimate of the value of network-level relationships between regions, held to a real caveat about how the connectome itself was actually built - see the page's citation-integrity note.

name: Behavioral reading/language measures
signal_examples: Trial-wise oral reading and lexical decision accuracy, reaction time, and errors for real-word and pseudoword corpora
citation: Anderson, E. J., Staples, R., Dyslin, S. M., Chang, E. H. T., Laks, A. B., Dickens, J. V., Mathur, D., Paul, S., Dvorak, E., & Turkeltaub, P. E. (2026). The Georgetown Reading in Aging Neuroimaging Dataset (GRAND) [Data set]. OpenNeuro. https://doi.org/10.18112/openneuro.ds007831.v1.0.1; Anderson, E. J. et al. (2026). The Georgetown Reading in Aging Neuroimaging Dataset (GRAND): Reading and multimodal MRI data in older adults. bioRxiv. https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.05.18.725986; Nautsch, A., Jimenez, A., Treiber, A., et al. (2019). Preserving privacy in speaker and speech characterisation. Computer Speech & Language, 58, 441-480. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.csl.2019.06.001
privacy_exit_point: Recorded via voice (oral reading trials) and response timing, outside the scanner; voice recordings carry their own re-identification risk, independent of any MRI modality.
agency_control_point: Conducted as a separate behavioral session outside the scanner; a participant can stop between trial blocks more readily than mid-scan, though the trial-wise design still requires many responses for the resulting summary measures to be usable.
notes: Illustrative gain/cost ratings, informed by the dataset's own description of its trial-wise design and by the cited voice-privacy literature, not values either source reports directly. Gain is rated highest of the five rows: this is the direct measurement of reading and language performance the imaging modalities are trying to explain, not an indirect neural correlate of it.
